name: Reza Pahlavi
role: Exiled former Crown Prince of Iran; claimant to the Iranian throne (born 1960)
summary: Pahlavi says Iran's future should be decided by its people, through a referendum on the form of the state and a secular democratic transition. He describes separation of religion and state, equal rights for citizens and women, and opposition to the Islamic Republic's repression. He has called for sanctions pressure, rejected outside military intervention in favour of civil resistance (later reportedly backing strikes), and proposed normalisation with Israel.

unions-good.rationale: A strike fund against the regime is nearby; no stated position on unions.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Reportedly called a March 2026 strike campaign a 'humanitarian intervention' against the regime, not Iran (secondhand report).

one-party-rule.rationale: Calls for free elections under international oversight and a democratic transition, opposing single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Says Iranians should choose between a constitutional monarchy and a republic by referendum, and that he would hold only a transitional role; his own preference is contested in reporting.

democracy-best.rationale: Calls for an elected government are nearby; the point about voters choosing badly is not addressed.

direct-votes.rationale: One referendum on the form of state is nearby; no stated position on direct votes on major laws.

right-to-secede.rationale: Says the territorial integrity of Iran is a red line and warned against a Kurdish alliance seeking autonomy.

political-violence-never.rationale: Advocates nonviolent civil disobedience and says change must come from Iranians, yet in March 2026 he reportedly backed strikes on the IRGC.

separate-church-state.rationale: His transition plan rests on secularism and a firm separation of religion and state, to be ratified by national referendum.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: His plan rests on secularism and separation of religion and state, which rejects law based on scripture.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Calls for national unity are nearby; no stated position on ethnic composition of a nation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: States belief in inherent equal rights between men and women, opposing legally distinct public roles.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Promises that no aggressor or criminal will be safe from accountability before the law, through transitional justice.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: His plan guarantees individual rights and equality for all citizens.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal citizenship is a general principle; one civil law regardless of religion is not spelled out.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Calls for a national, democratic, elected government and a referendum as 'the ultimate expression of the people's will'.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Stresses that Iran's diverse ethnicities and religions have lived side by side and calls for national unity.

clerical-rule.rationale: Calls for a secular, democratic government and opposes rule by the Islamic Republic's clerical establishment.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Says Iran's nuclear weapons programme should be totally dismantled and that Iran has no need to weaponise it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Backed women protesting the mandatory dress code and said women should decide what to wear; a veil should be a free choice (reporter summary of his 2022 post).

ban-cartels.rationale: His transition plan would dismantle monopolies and rent-seeking (reporter paraphrase of a 2026 video message).

suppress-opposition.rationale: Calls for free elections under international oversight and a pluralistic transition, opposing suppression of opposition.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Calls for a national, democratic, elected government of the people and a secular state, placing authority with the people.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Dismantling Iran's weapons programme is nearby; Iran holds no arsenal, so unilateral disarmament is not addressed.

women-suffrage.rationale: States his belief in the inherent equal rights of men and women; his plan guarantees equal rights for citizens.

notes: Most of the 490 statements have no recorded position from his own words. The statement list has no sanctions item, so his support for 'maximum pressure' (Hudson 2020) is not answered. Death penalty: his office's calls to stop executions of protesters are not in an opened source and are not a general position, so the item is null. The Israel right-to-a-state item and the monarchy item are contested. His own monarchy preference is disputed in reporting (a 2024 BBC remark that he prefers a republic is not opened). Several opened sources are reporter paraphrase; medium/high answers rest on his quoted words in s1, s3, s4, s5, s10 and s12. Federalism, the economy, hijab in his own words beyond the 2022 post, and nuclear enrichment were not found in opened primary text. Full text of his books (Winds of Change, Gozashteh va Ayandeh) was not downloaded, so coverage is thinner than for a full-text audit.
